title: Direct scheduled and sporadic task-volume outcomes
contract: Dynamic scheduled waste and sporadic tasks, including hybrid discrete events, register each explicitly attached volume once. Requested volume equals pending plus completed-task plus failed-before-pickup plus unconfirmed-after-pickup volume. Return/duplicate callbacks cannot count fresh demand. New saved evidence contains component identity, coverage counts, grouped totals and per-task requests. Results Investigation checks generated rules/components/volumes, terminal outcomes, physical pickup evidence for failure phases, coverage of all tagged generated tasks, and exclusion from accumulated waste allocations. Known zero volume remains distinct from absent or old evidence.
limitations: These are recorded task outcomes, not independent reconstruction of configured demand or proof of physical disposal, decontamination or final staff handoff. Post-pickup failure is retained as unconfirmed task volume even if an intermediate physical arrival occurred. No automatic retry or stock restoration is inferred for direct events. Threshold pools, legacy waste, manual/timeframe tasks and tracked consumable quantities have separate scopes. Existing route-pair multiplicity applies; configured events and task records are not interchangeable.

title: Hybrid continuous and discrete demand without duplicate volume
contract: Hybrid uses continuous base volume for threshold collections and deterministic frequency events for separate direct tasks. Event volume is not also added to the threshold pool. Threshold and scheduled_threshold retain event-based filling; scheduled waste fills and frequency fills remain separate configured contributions in scheduled_threshold. Partial volume and closed-poll demand persist. One-hour references distinguish two legitimate components from the formerly duplicated third collection. Preview and four relevant editors explain mode semantics; category editors expose threshold event fields and plain scheduled waste disables unused frequency.
limitations: Hybrid totals remain runtime-dependent and no fixed hybrid preview total is claimed. Accumulated-waste balance covers its continuous threshold pool; direct sporadic and ordinary scheduled task volumes still require separate outcome accounting. Existing route-pair multiplicity and physical bin availability apply. This is a changed-result correction; historical runs retain their original frozen inputs and software identity.

title: Deterministic sporadic demand planning and retained events
contract: Sporadic and scheduled_sporadic modes accumulate deterministic fractional occurrences per 24 eligible hours, not random arrivals. Demand Preview shows poll-based releases and any clock-scheduled component in chronological order, with accrued/emitted/retained occurrence accounting and per-rule provenance. Missing valid route pairs retain whole events rather than discard them. Each emitted occurrence retains existing per-route-pair multiplicity. Inclusive final partial polls and the runtime minimum 60-second cadence apply. Independent Decimal arithmetic covers one route pair and unrestricted dates/hours; complex calendars use explicit hand-calculated references.
limitations: Preview does not dispatch, evaluate physical availability or simulate returns. Planned times precede configured runtime staggering. Additional tracked-stock demand and returns keep the overall total unknown. Hybrid/threshold modes remain runtime-dependent and their combined frequency/volume interactions need further audit. Preview bounds are 31 days, 20000 task records and 100000 sporadic poll evaluations. Retained events are generator state; they do not imply post-horizon retries or completed transport.

title: Legacy department waste outcome conservation
contract: Legacy accrued fill is allocated once to each collection. Failure before physical pickup restores fill once for a subsequent eligible poll; failure after pickup remains unconfirmed. Completion, failure and return callbacks cannot duplicate volume. Accrued equals residual plus pending plus completed plus unconfirmed. Restored attempts are diagnostic and not additional stock. Version 2 Results Investigation evidence includes explicitly identified dynamic and legacy generators, links legacy generation/outcome records and reconciles their allocations. Version 1 retains its dynamic-only scope.
limitations: Legacy per-department/stream rate and routing semantics are retained. This verifies modeled volume and task outcomes, not physical disposal or decontamination. A failure after pickup is not automatically retried because its physical arrival remains unknown. Restored fill is retried only on a later eligible generation poll within the demand horizon. Ordinary scheduled/sporadic demand remains outside accumulated-waste accounting. Broader mixed services, department stream override parity and inventory interactions remain open.

title: Tracked consumable stock and confirmed replenishment
contract: Continuous active-hour consumption is divided between department resources and retained across closing polls. Requests do not refill stock. Pending automatic requests suppress duplicates; scheduled top-ups deduct incoming supply. Confirmed completion/handoff credits ordered stock once, failure leaves stock depleted and permits retry. Top-up, full content exchange and replace-empty have distinct logical stock behavior. Initial plus delivered equals consumed plus removed plus remaining; unmet demand is recorded separately. Final balances, request states and confirmed delivery/handoff receipts are saved with coverage counts. Results Investigation reconciles per-item accounting against requests, terminal outcomes and matching physical arrivals; metrics link to contributing records. Old or partial receipt evidence remains unknown. Raw finite quantity contracts reject malformed input; ignored usage labels and mixed item routing are visible findings.
limitations: Stock is a per-rule/per-resource logical consumable balance, initially full, with unlimited supply at configured sources. Physical tote handling retains the existing exchange/handoff model; distinct handling workflows for each content mode are not established. Stock is credited at confirmed direct completion or at the existing staff-handoff commit, not backdated to its planned walking arrival. Consumption ends at the demand horizon while already requested supplies may arrive later. Mixed-source/mixed-payload requests and usage_rate-specific stochastic schedules are unsupported and warned. Cross-rule shared stock, partial deliveries, stock expiry and independent reconstruction of all consumption intervals remain open.

title: Accumulated waste allocation and outcome reconciliation
contract: Each pooled threshold funds one collection; alternative route pairs no longer multiply its volume. A pre-pickup failure restores its allocation exactly once for later retry. Completed collections, pending allocations, residual volume and post-pickup unconfirmed volume reconcile accrued demand. Return outcomes do not duplicate or restore collection volume. Recorded group and per-task allocation events with coverage counts drive Results Investigation metrics and event links. Totals and task outcomes are cross-checked; missing evidence stays unknown.
limitations: Balance covers dynamic accumulated volume and threshold collections, not ordinary scheduled/sporadic work, legacy waste, tracked-item consumption or physical disposal. Post-pickup failures remain unconfirmed; recovery-to-volume reconciliation is not implemented. Cancelled/partial/older logs have unknown full coverage. Candidate-route selection is deterministic round-robin per pool among the triggering rule's valid pairs; it does not model a spatial waste distribution within that pool.

title: Initial bins follow resolved active Waste rules
contract: Modern Waste seeding uses the existing generator resolver for effective pickup, payload, group identity and initial presence. Disabled department/stream/group contributors cannot choose stock. A globally disabled enabled-modern definition seeds no rule-owned bins. Active contributors alone participate in shared-definition conflicts. Automatic shared groups use the full pickup signature and seed one bin at the first viable configured pickup; full cycles preserve that ID. Unavailable seed space creates no replacement stock and waiting demand can expire. Department presence overrides category defaults. Legacy/custom seed behavior remains on an explicit adapter.
limitations: Legacy/custom services without an enabled modern Waste definition retain the raw seed adapter. Multiple independent department bins, orphaned references and all inventory priority combinations remain unaudited. Threshold failure restoration, multi-pair waste-volume accounting and tracked-item consumption remain open; physical bin conservation does not prove waste-volume conservation.

title: Shared physical bin identity, delayed return and definition checks
contract: Department payload overrides seed the correct bin. Grouped tasks cannot borrow another group at the same pickup. Forced same-instance returns retain delay and route profile even without a generic return payload, including tasks bound after the bin returns. Failed outbound travel retains the bin at source; failed return retains it at destination, and waiting demand expires without duplicating it. Active dynamic shared contributors must agree on resolved payload, capacity, threshold and initial-presence flag; structured checks and runtime reject disagreements. One-route scheduled references conserve physical identities through editor import.
limitations: Raw seed definitions still differ from resolved demand rules: category/group inheritance, inactive seed contributors, automatic multi-pickup grouping, limited inventory spaces and legacy lifecycle combinations remain unaudited. Threshold volume is consumed when collection is generated, not proof of completed transport; failure restoration and multi-pair volume conservation remain open. Forced seeded returns still inherit outbound profiles when their return profile is blank.

title: Waste threshold precedence and legacy conservation
contract: Dynamic derived thresholds use effective capacity and fraction after department stream overrides, while positive explicit thresholds win. Compatible shared contributors reconcile accrued volume to collected plus residual volume; separate bins stay separate. Legacy polls retain closed-time fill, decimal equality creates the correct number of collections, and invalid routes retain volume without incrementing task counts. Dynamic invalid routes also retain fill. Plain editor import preserves legacy enablement and priority without injecting an enabled modern Waste template. Shared flags and waste dimensions have raw checks.
limitations: Does not establish complete physical bin/return lifecycle, incompatible shared definitions or multi-pair collection semantics. Legacy demand-dialog migration and waste coefficients remain to be audited; global definitions still control legacy thresholds. Earlier provenance screenshot documents historical arithmetic and is superseded by the new review.

title: Calendar-aware accumulated demand and conservation
contract: Accumulation integrates category-active and department-open time across each polling interval. Polls at closing retain prior eligible demand; inactive weekdays and fortnight blocks add no volume. Pending threshold and sporadic work releases on a later eligible poll, including when no new demand accrued. Reference arithmetic conserves collected plus residual volume and fractional event counts. Numerical equality tolerances prevent missing decimal collections/events. Shared raw checks reject malformed rates; preview explains that continuous volume alone does not trigger collections.
limitations: Release times remain poll-dependent. Reference tests cover dynamic single-pair rules; shared waste pools, legacy generators, tracked-item consumption/resets and complete hybrid interactions remain open. A no-work preview is not a stock or physical payload-conservation proof.

title: Active-date allocation and explicit calendar exclusions
contract: Timeframe pool membership considers actual eligible dates throughout a window, including overnight weekday and fortnight transitions. Existing group ordinal semantics and release-date filtering remain; excluded slots are not redistributed. Independent references cover disjoint department calendars, closed members, partial horizons and raw/editor parity. Imported missing category/department weekdays retain unrestricted runtime behavior and dialogs display all seven days. Demand Preview records candidate-slot dispositions and reconciles eligible versus emitted records with explicit exclusions.
limitations: Slot accounting uses generator decisions and is not an independent expected-result calculation. Group ordinals do not book staff or optimise a shared calendar; differently sized department windows can overlap in release time. Accumulation-mode calendars, all malformed weekday inputs, global fixed-staff empty-day semantics and complete schema coverage remain open.

title: Overnight and disjoint working periods with visible fallback
contract: Timeframe release spreading uses the union of all applicable staff/department periods, including overnight carry-in, with no closed-gap or overlap double counting. Equal staff start/end means closed, consistent with runtime. Department group counts include overnight openings from a previous active day. No staff overlap preserves configured demand with explicit fallback reasons and preview counts; it does not authorise out-of-hours handling. Department opening at the exclusive deadline yields zero work with an explicit explanation. Rotating weekday restrictions are ignored consistently and reported as unsupported.
limitations: Spreading does not book staff or guarantee deadlines. Heterogeneous pooled calendars and category active-day/fortnight transitions remain to be accepted; runtime still has a flagged bounded-search fallback. Only the delivered reference scope is independently verified, not every calendar combination or all no-work modes.

title: Shared generation input validation and unsupported cycles
contract: Raw editor import, simulator construction and direct task-manager entry share checks for generation flags, mode names, selected counts/durations, staff patterns and custom hours. Malformed values fail with exact field paths before coercion; a rejected generation-settings edit leaves the store unchanged. Project checks expose custom work/rest cycles as unsupported warnings requiring acknowledgement, with dependency tracking invalidating old evidence after edits. Valid numeric strings, false/omission, zero polling intervals and named department waste-stream references retain compatibility.
limitations: Bounded validation rather than a complete schema. Unknown fields, all policy names, scheduling semantics, weekday lists and complete effective-rule interactions remain unaudited. Direct lower-level generator classes and static task metadata are not comprehensively validated. CLI constructors reject errors; unsupported warnings require the Project checks workflow for acknowledgement. Full feature inventory and application gate remain open.

title: Global staff switches and consistent timeframe releases
contract: Generation and runtime share effective staff-choice resolution, including legacy Stores labels, source, payload and generated IDs. Disabling global patterns gives generated tasks one all-day roster without disabling staff; custom weekly hours remain effective. The independent spread switch controls timeframe release distribution within global/custom hours. Fixed scheduled releases remain unchanged. Disabled patterns do not split otherwise shared custom-hour slots. Preview follows actual releases and no longer asserts an unspaced independent count for legacy staff demand.
limitations: Custom work/rest cycles, heterogeneous department-hour intersections within pooled timeframe groups, out-of-hours fallback policy and broad scalar validation remain open. Legacy direct/static task metadata is not rewritten. These checks do not establish optimal staffing or complete-run capacity.

title: Generated legacy staff tasks inherit working hours
contract: Generated tasks carry effective shift metadata independently of explicit or omitted staff choice. Runtime legacy Stores fallback now observes the same configured working periods as explicit true. False and non-Stores omission remain unstaffed; forced zone handoffs remain staffed. Independent raw/editor and full-simulation references reconcile staff finishes with return starts, including the existing saved return scenario.
limitations: Legacy direct tasks without shift metadata retain all-day availability. Custom work/rest cycles, mixed schedules and broad scalar validation remain open. Changed historical return timings require comparison with frozen earlier runs.

title: Staff travel and handling within alternating team blocks
contract: Valid four-day roster bookings constrain travel and handling to the selected team block, anchored to simulation start. A job that cannot fit moves to the incoming roster and recomputes its own travel and availability. Outgoing reservations and location history remain unchanged. Exact boundary finishes are permitted; overnight services cannot cross the team boundary. Incoming busy teams retain staffing expansion. An exhausted 35-day roster search retains the explicit working-hours fallback flag rather than looping indefinitely.
limitations: A flagged fallback is not verified capacity against working hours or team boundaries. Staffing remains conservative sizing, not capped queues or optimal rosters. Custom work/rest-day values are not used by the fixed four-day allocator. Heterogeneous patterns within one category and broader calendar interactions still need auditing.

title: Staff handling report reconciliation
contract: Reports include recorded handling and exchange events, preserve explicit Linen assignments and prefer logged initial roster counts and multipliers over configuration metadata. Task handling time is separate from the per-person union of recorded handling intervals. Missing person/interval evidence is unknown. Untracked department teams do not become invented headcount. New handling logs carry working-hours fallback and tracked-resource flags; legacy fallback status remains unavailable. Summary rows retain contributing event identifiers. Four-day team changes, return to team A, and work-period deferral across a team boundary have independent reference checks.
limitations: Recorded busy handling excludes travel and does not establish complete-run coverage or utilisation. Older timetables may still infer services from completion/return records and configured defaults; the new summary is not proof of their accuracy. Cross-boundary travel/overnight staffing, heterogeneous schedules in one pool, mixed tracked/untracked category rows and full metric navigation require further acceptance work.

title: Staff sizing and safe same-location batch bookings
contract: Independent reference bookings cover automatic pool expansion, shared overlapping services, travel waits, touching intervals, category pool identity, group override propagation, work-period deferral and explicit invalid-hours fallback. Stale batches cannot extend across a later booking; future batches do not delay earlier services; incoming work periods constrain shared finishes.
limitations: This is staffing sizing, not fixed-capacity queueing. No gap insertion or globally optimal staffing; nonchronological planning may overestimate headcount. Shared services retain historical per-task finishes, not one retroactively revised batch record. Full shift-team, lift-contention, busy-time and report reconciliation remain open.

title: Explicit staff choice and legacy omission
contract: Explicit false disables legacy Stores staff fallback; true enables it. Omission retains legacy fallback and survives editor roundtrips. Group false replaces category true. Actual staff records and completion-relative return delays reflect the effective choice. Physical zone handoffs still require staff.
limitations: Reference scope covers direct/static/generated choices and zone enforcement, not every staff scheduling/resource policy. Older normalised saved values cannot reveal whether a stored false was user-selected or inserted by an older version.

title: Generation precedence and imported return timing
contract: Category defaults are replaced by group/department fields; an empty group schedule suppresses category times and group membership suppresses standalone department work. Generated returns inherit the outbound profile only when the return-profile field is absent; explicit blank remains blank. Returns start after outbound arrival and configured delay, subject to staff handling. Imported rules no longer gain template staff flags or 15-minute handling when those fields are absent; new-project templates and explicit overrides remain.
limitations: Legacy Stores staff fallback, other omitted-template defaults, seeded/runtime waste returns and all generation modes still require broader auditing. Return counts are conditional and are not fixed demand-preview totals.

title: Routing flags and physical width input validation
contract: Project checks, editor loading and simulator construction share validation before normalisation. Routing flags require JSON booleans. Explicit widths must be finite and positive; all positive widths are preserved exactly, including below 0.1 m. Missing fields retain documented defaults; numeric width strings remain accepted.
limitations: This is a routing scalar boundary, not a complete configuration schema. Some interactive width controls still have a 0.1 m entry minimum. Old saved values already enlarged by previous versions cannot be reconstructed automatically.

title: Local route failure and endpoint preservation
contract: Valid local routes retain requested endpoints and clear expanded obstacle boxes. Invalid endpoints and exhausted bounded searches fail explicitly. Unsafe visual smoothing retains the clear polyline. Failed single and batch commitments restore resources.
limitations: Centreline and axis-aligned obstacle approximation only, not swept-footprint or radius validation. Unpositioned bays retain zero-movement behaviour. A bounded search failure does not prove global geometric infeasibility; alternative bay search is incomplete.

title: Application source binding for prepared runs
contract: Root and visualiser/report Python sources are fingerprinted. Changed, added or deleted sources invalidate prepared execution; historical results remain readable with an explicit older-scope warning.
limitations: Conservative application source binding, not a tamper-proof audit. Third-party packages and Python runtime are not part of this source fingerprint.

title: Routing and door defaults and option traceability
contract: Sixteen routing/door options have explicit runtime defaults, editor/import behaviour, precedence, validation boundaries, source symbols, support disposition and linked acceptance results. Directed/profile/width constraints compose; omitted auto-connect is retained on import and uses runtime true, whereas new editor projects explicitly store false.
limitations: Other option families still need individual audit. Seeded/runtime return interactions and UI width-entry consistency remain open. Passing linked cases does not promote partial behaviour to complete support.

title: Route-profile identification and access preview
contract: Layout and frozen-run playback share profile labels, contrast-checked colours, line patterns and direction arrows. Shared sections display every permitted profile; clean/dirty/shared remains defined by route profiles. The searchable table projects explicit and automatic same-floor graph access, combining node and directed-edge allowances with physical directions. Empty lists are unrestricted. Automatic reverse connections retain direction provenance. Lift allowances are listed separately and do not block same-floor transit at lift nodes. Malformed input disables the preview visibly; removed selections switch off. Styles persist per user by profile name without changing project/check/revision/run inputs. Playback uses frozen profile data. Independent directed reference cases, simulator agreement, styling/persistence, map interaction and large-text controls pass.
limitations: This is a permission projection, not a trajectory or feasibility assessment. Direct-travel fallback, task-local additions, combined loads, clearance, outages and timing are not displayed. Lift journeys are not same-floor corridors. Dense labels need zoom/filtering; automatic collision avoidance and standalone legacy viewer controls remain open. Schematic parallel strokes are not verified lanes or swept geometry.

title: Per-user accessible display preferences
contract: Project Appearance provides Light, Dark and High contrast presets, 8-24 pt interface text, 10-28 px layout text, custom text/accent/map colours and a visible or hidden map legend. Preferences persist separately from project/revision/run inputs. Existing standard controls are repolished and new controls inherit the palette/font. Active text is checked at 4.5:1 against preset backgrounds, accent at 3:1; selected text uses whichever of black/white has greater contrast. Invalid drafts do not apply, corrupt settings fall back visibly without overwriting, and failed saves retain active preferences. Apply does not alter project data, history or check currency. Pending property drafts survive. Reference contrast, persistence, live controls, keyboard actions and 1280x800 large-text behaviour are tested.
limitations: Playback map labels, timelines, drawings and some legacy custom controls retain existing rendering. Arbitrary underlays are outside contrast checks. Complete keyboard/screen-reader and dialog coverage, route-profile labels/patterns/colour preferences and accessibility compliance are not established.

title: Explicit recovery of staged containers
contract: A direct recovery task names an exact issued container staged at its pickup and marked as requiring recovery. It claims the container exclusively, applies ordinary robot, route-profile and destination-capacity checks, and moves it at scheduled pickup/dropoff. Rejection restores claims; failed recovery before pickup leaves staging intact, while failure after pickup records unconfirmed arrival. Confirmed arrival preserves physical identity/state and closes the outstanding recovery finding. Tasks UI exposes identity and recovery and preserves unrelated options.
limitations: Recovery is configured for a new run; it does not mutate frozen logs or resume a completed run. No unidentified or unconfirmed object is recovered. Staging geometry/capacity and direct recovery combined with staff handoffs or further automatic returns are unsupported. Existing manual-task robot compatibility rules apply.

title: Same-floor graph routing
contract: Euclidean edge lengths unless distance_m is supplied; directed edges remain directed; distance divided by constant speed gives travel time.
limitations: Reference cases do not prove all graph shapes or validate surveyed distances.

title: Door and corridor straight-passage width
contract: Passage requires max(robot width, oriented payload width) <= effective edge width, with 1e-9 m numerical tolerance. Effective width is the minimum of the corridor and its endpoint door openings. Select the shortest passable route.
limitations: No safety clearance, door height, opening time, door leaf swing or swept turning footprint is modelled. A door restricts both full incident edges.

title: Route profiles and task restrictions
contract: Route profiles define clean, dirty and shared access: shared sections belong to each applicable profile. Profile and task allow-lists are unioned; empty lists mean unrestricted; edge pairs are directed. The dirty task label selects the dirty profile only when no explicit profile is supplied. Unknown effective profiles reject scheduling instead of becoming unrestricted. Empty approach, charging and idle-return travel remain unrestricted by profiles. Returns use return_route_profile or their label fallback; seeded waste returns may inherit the outbound profile. Generating profile edges from selected nodes includes both directions of two-way corridors. Each multi-stop leg intersects the effective permissions of payloads currently onboard; empty intersections remain forbidden. Clearance uses only the oriented payloads currently carried. Profile/task unions remain per-task; batch groups retain profile and dirty-label compatibility.
limitations: No physical contamination-state model or empty-journey profile selector. Task allowances can widen a profile intentionally. Reference node, edge and lift intersections are verified; seeded-return and wider profile interactions remain incomplete. Static checks do not resolve every effective generation or runtime-return profile; the engine checks effective tasks before scheduling. Existing saved edge lists are not automatically changed; regenerate deliberately if reverse directions were omitted.

title: Corridor lane capacity
contract: Current two-way capacity approximation uses half corridor width and both loaded length and width to choose one or two concurrent lanes.
limitations: Not a directional keep-right lane model; no geometric junction conflict or overtaking verification. Length-based lane fitting is conservative.

title: Swept turns and multi-point manoeuvres
contract: Planned shared geometric model with explicit radius, pivot and reversing parameters.
limitations: Existing local manoeuvre drawing uses an approximate radius. Do not treat it as verified full-route swept geometry or steering dynamics.

title: Scheduled generation and override precedence
contract: Global disable wins. Enabled group/department rules can run under disabled category defaults. Group payload overrides category values and suppresses that department's standalone override. Separate groups are separate services. Category-wide zone capacity policy overrides ordinary group/department values; later department waste-stream settings are an existing exception. Category-only generation runs only without groups or department overrides. Polling includes the final partial interval at the inclusive demand horizon; released work can complete afterward. Clock schedules and timeframe slots now use exact calendar events. Effective pre-start releases are excluded; department opening adjustments can retain an occurrence across midnight. Consumption polling cadence is unchanged.
limitations: Exact release does not imply immediate assignment: resource waits, staff handoffs and configured staggering remain. Minute clock parsing is retained; fractional timeframe slots retain calculated precision. The wider generation-mode and calendar interaction matrix is still incomplete.

title: Consumption, threshold, waste and timeframe generation
contract: Generation derives demand from schedules, configured consumption and department assignments; tracked containers have separate balances.
limitations: Independent boundary cases remain for every mode, recurrence, waste volume, partial-day and timeframe allocation. Preview must distinguish runtime-dependent demand from fixed schedules.

title: Task assignment, priorities and deferral
contract: Deferral deadline starts at the original release and applies until assignment; zero means unlimited. Idle parking is excluded. One reference delivery takes 2 + 10/2 + 2 = 9 seconds.
limitations: Priority fairness, all candidate-limit interactions and end-of-run incomplete-task reconciliation need further reference cases.

title: Returns, staff handoffs and exchanges
contract: Returns and staff transfers retain physical payload identities. Same-container servicing records an arrival outside storage and returns the original bin; finite exchange stock is unaffected. Destination dwell and walking contribute separately to availability.
limitations: Existing regression coverage is broad, but a complete independent return/profile/staff-shift matrix is outstanding.

title: Location reservation capacity
contract: Reservations occupy half-open intervals. A request starts at the earliest time that existing simultaneous occupancy stays below capacity throughout its duration.
limitations: These tests cover location reservations, not all lift, edge, staff or junction contention.

title: Inventory bays and payload instances
contract: Flexible bays accept matching dimensions with permitted plan rotation. Exchange deliveries and returns can represent different physical instances. Same-bin service arrivals do not create stored stock or consume a finite bay. Strict multi-stop deliveries require distinct compatible bays. Existing active claims cannot be overwritten. Temporarily full compatible bays wait until capacity is released or the original deferral deadline expires; without a deadline they can remain pending. Finite full-bin exchange plans claim distinct existing empty instances at commit, retain them in storage until outbound arrival, consume only their owned claim, and release unconsumed claims on rejection or task failure. Physical pickup/dropoff are scheduled independently of journey completion, including batch legs and post-delivery washing; completion fallbacks are idempotent. Equivalent-bin exchange requires an enabled return. Without it, deliveries need ordinary free storage and cannot consume empty stock. Tasks requiring existing source stock claim distinct physical instances at serial route commitment; estimates remain non-binding, rejected commits restore claims and task bindings, and pickup/failure releases owned claims. Exact and empty-only pickups take precedence over flexible selection; source pickups and empty exchanges cannot share an instance. Delivered stock can be collected again. An explicit ID on an ordinary outbound task creates at most one physical object: committed creation is exclusive, issued IDs require existing stock at the requested source, and in-transit or removed objects cannot be recreated. Creation claims roll back or release on failure before pickup. Generated IDs skip registered explicit IDs. Conflicting task payload types for one ID are preflight errors. Physical payload checks reject malformed dimensions, mass, preferences and duplicate/reserved identities before import or simulation. Runtime and editor share bay dimension inference: resolved template heights include legacy/default payload dimensions, modern fields precede aliases, flexibility aliases survive import, and inferred dimensions retain precision. Project Checks exposes unused payload and bay volume metadata. Shared bay checks reject malformed inputs and duplicate resolved names before coercion; unknown payload/AMR restrictions block running instead of silently broadening compatibility. The bay setter validates atomically, preserves dimension-only and legacy short-outline bays, retains precision/metadata, and uses shared envelope inference. Occupancy markers are explicitly distinguished from seeded physical stock in Project Checks.
limitations: Reference cycles verify instance conservation and storage counts; system-wide conservation over long mixed workflows still needs independent evidence. Explicit staging geometry/capacity remains open. Direct staged recovery is verified in PAYLOAD-RECOVERY-01; unconfirmed locations cannot be recovered. Internal same-bin and staged-equivalent returns retain their existing continuation policies. Lifecycle counts distinguish planned, stored, in-transit, staged, unconfirmed and removed IDs. Physical population peaks include active issued objects; final identity records support state totals. Failed returns preserve staged identities and flag recovery needs. Staff-action timing and full mixed-workflow lifecycle coverage remain incomplete. Bay fit remains an axis-aligned envelope with plan rotation and 1e-6 metre tolerance; complete polygon geometry, mixed AMR/payload classification, legacy slot aliases, location schema, zero-dimension policy and the legacy unknown-height sentinel remain under audit.

title: AMR types, slots and multi-stop routing
contract: Robot and slot dimensions constrain payload compatibility; multi-stop tasks share movements. Each multi-stop leg intersects the effective permissions of payloads currently onboard; empty intersections remain forbidden. Clearance uses only the oriented payloads currently carried. Profile/task unions remain per-task; batch groups retain profile and dirty-label compatibility. Rejected serial multi-stop commits restore touched reservations, inventory claims, lift operational state, battery/energy and impact counters. Rejected individual and idle-return commits also restore task destinations, robot state and appended charging records. Shared raw/editor slot resolution preserves legacy dimension fallbacks and explicit slot precedence. Input checks reject malformed capacities, robot scalars, quantities, flags, duplicate identities/slot names and empty or unknown orientation permissions. Legacy comma-separated orientations resolve consistently for payload and slot. Exact capacity boundaries and permission intersections are independently tested. Project checks expose ignored per-type start locations and the robot-mass energy limitation.
limitations: Slot combinations, fleet contention, routing optimality and all orientation combinations need further cases. Greedy pickup-first stop ordering is not a complete tour search. Swept slot geometry is not verified. Distinct empty-bin claims are verified; atomicity beyond route planning remains a separate audit. Legacy size capacity is a per-dimension fallback, not volume. No independent aggregate structural payload mass limit or multi-slot geometric packing model is established. Physical payload scalar validation beyond orientation remains a separate audit.

title: Battery, charging and idle returns
contract: Opportunity charging is optional and admits idle robots progressively. Rejected charging-route plans retain departure occupancy and restore charger claims, lift operational state and robot targets. Estimates do not assign a target charger. One in-place charge reference verifies 10 kWh / 2 kW = 18000 seconds. Charger travel reserves corridor capacity, spends 75% of rated motor power over corridor movement, and recharges from arrival energy. Explicit waits consume no traction energy; lift energy is recorded separately and not deducted from the AMR battery on charger trips. Available battery may cross the reserve threshold but cannot be exceeded. The legacy recharge entry point uses charge-cycle events. Delivery and batch traction now uses corridor/local-manoeuvre durations and actual onboard load; explicit waits and lift travel consume no AMR traction. Lift supply includes boarding standby and is recorded once per journey. Exact committed traction must leave the battery reserve intact; estimates do not spend battery. At an operational charger, an individual delivery whose constructed route exceeds current battery but fits a full battery is retried after charging. The abandoned commit is rolled back, then routing and reservations are recomputed at the later time. Charging, pickup/dropoff and completion share one timeline. When no delivery is assignable, an eligible idle robot can request charging for route energy even above reserve. Each available compatible charger is checked for reachable arrival and a feasible full-battery onward task; commitment rechecks the selected destination. The original task stays pending and records route_charge_required evidence. Charger availability inspection is read-only; stale markers are cleaned only during serial claims. Investigation and report analysis share a source-attributed movement ledger: native event IDs count once, and complete bound logs with the energy capability distinguish known zero from missing evidence. Multi-stop task energy is unallocated; shared journey totals remain explicitly labelled. Transport groups containing shared journeys leave task energy blank. PDF lift totals use the same evidence and preserve unknowns. Planned recharge segments record input separately from applied battery credits. Complete bound logs reconcile each expected robot: initial plus applied charge minus traction equals final model energy, with separate counter checks. In-place charge credits occur at route commitment; separate cycles credit on completion. Missing or cancelled evidence remains unknown. Duplicate event IDs count once; conflicting duplicates are rejected. Explicit charger bays are reserved before travel and occupied at arrival. Separate charge-cycle IDs reject stale or duplicate events. Arrival and completion recheck charger validity and ownership; rejected cycles credit no energy. Busy chargers and failed charging attempts are operational events, not delivery task failures. Earlier delivery completions cannot clear a newer charging reservation. Identical local position and heading require zero movement.
limitations: Energy remains approximate: no stationary AMR auxiliary draw or robot own mass in the lift equation; rated-power/load formula is not a measured vehicle model. Fast assignment and pre-charge estimates omit some traffic and local-bay effects; exact individual-route shortfalls now replan in-place charging, and dispatch from non-chargers is covered by bounded references. Direct batch charging now replans the whole tour at the later departure, rolling back the original attempt. Charger detours check the entire onward batch and serial availability. Feasible deliveries precede detours; charged batches retain multi-stop preference among detours. Whole-fleet optimisation remains outstanding. Full-battery infeasibility is a route-attempt finding, not proof that every future route is impossible. One-bay/two-robot contention and fault-injected bay losses are verified. FIFO queues, idle-full-robot relocation, continuously monitored charger faults, partial charge after interruption, efficiency and wider threshold boundaries remain open. Locations without explicit bays retain legacy unbounded charging. Per-task batch energy allocation is deliberately unspecified; use movement events once for journey totals. Energy is route-plan consumption, not independently measured execution, and charging input is excluded from this movement ledger. Legacy logs lack corrected segment attribution. Atomicity after route planning and full report reconciliation remain separate audits.

title: Lift simulation and movement exports
contract: Lift transfers and empty repositioning are distinct movements; multiple tasks on one movement do not multiply its count. Reposition and loaded speeds are sampled at their planned start times. Committed routes remain fixed. Wear/failure-enabled lifts book in chronological commitment order; with both disabled, gaps are allowed only when the new recorded journey restores the next booking's original starting floor. No unrecorded reset movement is assumed. Committed journeys apply wear once; estimates do not. Rejected commits restore wear, repair and reservations. Deterministic failures use accumulated vertical operating time and a post-wear health-scaled threshold; boarding, doors and waits are excluded. Zero threshold disables failures; zero repair time still records a failure. Repair does not restore health; the minimum operating-health boundary is inclusive. Results Investigation checks per-lift recorded floor continuity and exclusive movement intervals, with a 2 ms rounding tolerance, against frozen initial floors and booking-derived transfer/reposition counts. Conflicts link to native events; full known-zero coverage requires the new count capability and valid complete evidence. Legacy or filtered observations remain explicitly incomplete. Shared scalar checks reject malformed lift timing, envelope, energy and reliability inputs before simulation. Floors/second is authoritative; lift displays show its physical equivalent and preflight warns about stale metres/second metadata. Editor saves avoid three-decimal floors/second rounding and omitted cabin/boarding defaults agree with runtime. Lift floor definitions are checked before import or execution: unique IDs, unique integer served floors, served start floor, exactly matching canonical floor-position keys, finite coordinates and noncolliding generated graph names. Missing fields can remain in editor drafts but block run checks. Rename collisions are rejected before callbacks mutate the project.
limitations: Commitment-order scheduling can leave gaps unused and can delay a robot behind an already booked later arrival. Dynamic replanning of committed journeys is not implemented. Mid-phase outage/speed integration, multiple-lift interactions, stochastic failures and complete report reconciliation remain unverified or unsupported. Health and repair state represent committed work rather than elapsed-time sensor state. Project Checks exposes these scheduling and reliability assumptions. Cabin fit uses max robot/payload dimensions rather than swept or stacked geometry. Legacy size-unit capacity has no fit/concurrency effect; no rated cabin mass or independent multi-robot co-occupancy is implemented. Valid rename/floor-removal reference migration and all editor range/precision round trips remain under audit; per-floor entrance positions need not align into a physical shaft.

title: People movement and congestion
contract: Configured people occupancy applies speed factors to corridor travel.
limitations: No dedicated independent reference suite for overlapping profiles, ramp shapes or time windows yet.

title: Scenarios and resource availability
contract: Scenario events modify selected resource availability and speed over configured periods. Scheduled boundaries wake pending work and invalidate estimates. Individual, batch and separate charging admission respect robot outages. Structural lift feasibility is independent of temporary availability. Windows are half-open and overnight weekdays belong to the start day; equal clocks mean all day. Original task deferral deadlines remain in force.
limitations: Already committed work is not interrupted. Mid-journey outages, chained corridor closures, lift repair/wear, speed-only interactions, DST and full malformed-input validation remain outstanding. Partial availability retains a speed-factor approximation, not stochastic uptime. Recovery boundaries are limited to the configured demand horizon.

title: Run period and simulation time
contract: Simulation times are elapsed seconds relative to the configured start datetime. Individual exports may round times.
limitations: Timezone/DST, all midnight boundaries and all end-of-run semantics need explicit policy and reference cases. tick_rate is not a physical accuracy setting.

title: Reports and metric reconciliation
contract: Tasks, AMR journeys, payload movements and lift trips are separate measures. Missing metadata must not be fabricated.
limitations: Complete metric-to-event traceability and reconciliation for every report measure remain outstanding.

title: PDF/DXF drawing import and export
contract: Drawings provide floor-scaled underlays; topology uses explicit world coordinates.
limitations: No automatic verified obstacle extraction from drawings. Broader import failure/scale coverage remains.

title: Editor validation and dialog behaviour
contract: Structured preflight reports severity, object, consequences and navigation. Exact known paths select common object/field properties, including parallel corridor records; stale indices and ambiguous point identities cannot select the wrong object. Per-finding input dependencies and evaluated/skipped check groups distinguish changed inputs from unchanged inputs. Returning through the workflow tree retains the old report until explicit recheck. All configuration changes still invalidate whole-run readiness and observed stale checks clear warning acknowledgements. Referenced drawing availability and project-folder changes invalidate live checks. Unknown and legacy checks retain conservative whole-project dependencies. Additive metadata preserves finding IDs and original schema-1 fields. Launcher snapshots checked inputs, findings, dependency evidence and warnings per run. Existing dialogs remain available. Shared compressed edit history supports undo/redo of completed configuration and canvas edits.
limitations: Incremental checks, not a complete schema. Generation rule references need effective precedence resolution; legacy findings may lack exact navigation, and fields absent from contextual properties still require full editors. Drawing checks cover path availability, not content validity. File checks and storage remain synchronous. Undo groups existing dialogs and callbacks; individual command migration and systematic accessibility coverage remain outstanding.

title: Visualiser and task investigation
contract: Playback uses event records; failure navigation locates the affected destination.
limitations: Legacy playback remains supported. Results investigation adds evidence IDs and task timelines; shared swept trajectories and full report reconciliation remain outstanding.

title: Portable project, history and integrated application
contract: Compressed .amrproj stores deduplicated drawings and revisions with atomic saves and restore. Separate 30-second recovery copies preserve unsaved configurations and available drawings; Save/Discard/Cancel protects open/close. JSON export serves existing tools; results remain external. Project runs saves, checks and simulates a frozen saved revision in a separate process, with external results bound to project, revision and software identities. Optional versioned archive metadata persists external results roots and run references without embedding outputs or creating configuration revisions. Accepted new runs and relinks save atomically. Relative paths support moving a project/results bundle; Save As rebases links to existing folders. Missing references remain visible; relinking validates the selected run, revision/configuration and software identities. Metadata saves preserve unsaved configuration edits. Older archives without links open unchanged. A persistent workflow tree hosts Project, Layout, Configuration, Check, Simulate, Review and Report in one central workspace. Existing checks, demand, history, run and investigation panels are reused against shared state. Selected runs flow into investigation and reporting. Reports verify full bound logs and frozen inputs, run in a separate process, retain source/report software checksums, and remain external. Cancelled or failed reports cannot be opened as completed outputs. Review embeds revision-bound playback with a local timeline and monitors, read-only background loading, native event identities, independent reference positions, and stale-selection/project-switch guards. Playback pauses on leaving the workspace. Current edits cannot change frozen run inputs. Layout has a searchable object tree and contextual position, door, corridor and location-wash properties. Changed fields apply atomically with bulk previews and one-step undo; valid drafts are included in recovery. Stale drafts cannot overwrite newer edits. Robots, payloads, lifts, static tasks and route profiles have tree entries and common contextual fields. Route permissions use searchable node, directed-edge and lift selections, with explicit unrestricted-empty semantics. Untouched nested settings and identities are preserved. Lift speed edits synchronize floors/s with the legacy m/s representation.
limitations: Playback drawing underlays, interruptible/paged large-log loading, nested configuration editing and object creation/deletion/renaming, broader identity/floor editing, removal/retention controls and large-project responsiveness remain outstanding. Configuration tools still use existing dialogs. Report generation is integrated, but PDF viewing uses the system viewer and complete metric reconciliation remains open. Storage/discovery operations are synchronous. Older builds may discard optional metadata; complete migration coverage remains open. The legacy launcher retains its machine-specific workspace path.

title: Demand preview and rule provenance
contract: Frozen planned-task preview with filters, timetable, effective rule settings, no-work explanations and simple independent schedule reconciliation. Dynamic rules record ordered category, group, department and waste-stream assignments, including equal-value overrides, source paths and derived calculations. Effective settings exposes field histories; older and inactive rules do not invent sources. Runtime-dependent totals remain unknown.
limitations: Complex calendars, runtime inventory/returns, task-specific adjustments, global staff settings, inactive rules and implicit defaults still need complete attribution and independent verification. Waste threshold derivation now uses effective department overrides; department stream settings can still override category-wide policy after its restoration. Preview IDs are not simulation event IDs.

title: Results timelines and run evidence
contract: Recorded task outcomes and metric definitions link to contributing events. New logs retain stable event/journey identities, frozen inputs and source fingerprints; old logs expose missing evidence. Completed and failed task sets reconcile with bound run summaries. Payload service arrivals close transfers without adding inventory; logs declare this capability so older logs do not claim zero service activity. Failures after pickup and before dropoff record an unconfirmed physical arrival; no source stock or destination arrival is fabricated. Failed batch members cannot later complete. New full logs publish final lifecycle identities; investigation metrics link state and issued totals to those records. Missing lifecycle evidence remains unknown. Report task counts are independent of physical IDs; missing ID or physical-population evidence is not substituted with task or stored counts. Results Investigation checks per-lift recorded floor continuity and exclusive movement intervals, with a 2 ms rounding tolerance, against frozen initial floors and booking-derived transfer/reposition counts. Conflicts link to native events; full known-zero coverage requires the new count capability and valid complete evidence. Legacy or filtered observations remain explicitly incomplete.
limitations: Planned segments do not prove execution. Payload pairing can be incomplete; wait causes are not additive; full PDF metric reconciliation and large-log pagination remain open.

title: Corridor drawing, splitting and subdivision
contract: Selected explicit same-floor corridors can be divided into 2Ã¢â‚¬â€œ100 sections, or split at a projected click. Directed edges share inserted nodes and retain attributes. Configured distance is divided proportionally; geometric paths stay on the original line. Route-profile and task allowances, people corridor references and scenario corridor resources are updated atomically. Original doors stay at their endpoints. One undo restores the complete configuration. Clean/dirty/shared access remains defined by route profiles. Continuous drawing previews and atomically places, reuses or joins points, automatically linking each click with per-step undo. Point/edge snapping precedes grid rounding. Finishing or changing floor/mode/history clears the active chain. New links honor the bidirectional choice; existing links retain their permissions. New branches are not implicitly granted restricted profile access.
limitations: Added graph sections can change reservation and people-occupancy timing; identical congested outcomes are not promised. Auto-generated links must first be explicit. Crossing lines do not implicitly join; an overlapping target selects one corridor, not all crossings. Configurable snap tolerances, dedicated crossing operations, geometric traffic and all effective generated-rule interactions remain open. Historical links are not migrated for the former direction-checkbox defect.
